newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor, Zaire reach agreement on Kamoto.
newsitem.headline: Iscor, Zaire reach agreement on Kamoto.

text.p: Zaire's Gecamines has awarded South African iron and steel producer Iscor Ltd the right to complete a feasibility study for the rehabilitation of the Kamoto Underground Mine in Shaba Province, Iscor said on Sunday.
Subject to the results of the feasibility study, Iscor has also obtained the rights to raise capital for and implemnt the project, Iscor said in a statement.

"Iscor Mining...has reached a cooperation agreement with Gecamines, the State Mining Corporation of Zaire...which gives Iscor the right to complete a feasibility study for the rehabilitation of the Kamoto Underground Mine in Shaba Province, Southern Zaire," Iscor said.
Iscor Mining's managing director Ben Alberts said that the copper and cobalt reserves at Kamoto were estimated at 66 million tonnes, grading 4.4 percent copper and 0.5 percent cobalt.

"Subject to the successful completion of the feasibility study, the raising of the necessary financing and guarantees, it is conceivable that rehabilitation of the Kamoto Mine could start as early as the fourth quarter of 1997," Iscor said.
The South African corporation said it and Gecamines aimed to return the mine to its previous output levels of a minimum of two million tonnes of ore per annum in as short a time as possible.
